avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin/Anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Etodolac inhibits platelet function and increases bleeding risk; additive anticoagulant effect
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if unavoidable, monitor INR closely and adjust warfarin dose

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Aspirin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Combined NSAID use increases GI ulceration, bleeding, and cardiovascular risk
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine; use only one NSAID at a time

avoid_supplements.name: Corticosteroids
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Synergistic increase in GI ulceration and bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid combination; if necessary, use lowest effective doses and monitor GI symptoms

avoid_supplements.name: Feverfew
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both inhibit platelet aggregation; increased bleeding risk

caution_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild platelet inhibition may have additive antiplatelet effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for signs of bleeding; use moderate amounts only

caution_supplements.name: Ginger
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet properties; potential additive effect
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased bleeding tendency; culinary amounts generally safe

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet activity; potential additive GI irritation
caution_supplements.action: Monitor GI tolerance; doses >1g daily warrant caution

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (>2 drinks/day)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases GI irritation, ulceration risk, and hepatotoxicity
avoid_foods.action: Limit alcohol to ≤1 drink/day or avoid entirely; counsel on GI bleeding risk

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay etodolac absorption and increase GI distress
caution_foods.action: Take etodolac with food or milk to minimize GI upset, but avoid excessive fat

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase GI irritation and stomach acid; CYP1A2 substrate interaction potential
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine intake; monitor for increased GI symptoms

monitoring_notes: Monitor for GI bleeding, ulceration, renal function, and blood pressure during etodolac therapy. Assess for drug interactions affecting CYP2C9 metabolism and counsel on cardiovascular/thrombotic risk, particularly in patients with history of MI or stroke.
